arabic.text: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ (١) وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ (٢) لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍۢ (٣) تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍۢ (٤) سَلَٰمٌ هِىَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ (٥)

questions.q: Recite 97:1 and name three rules in it.
questions.a: Ghunnah on «إِنَّآ», madd munfasil, ikhfa' in «أَنزَلْنَٰهُ», qalqalah at «ٱلْقَدْرِ».

questions.q: Tajweed map (pupil PDF): label every rule in Al-Qadr. Today's rota group recites An-Naba' 1 to 8.
questions.a: At least ten rules labelled, as on the slide plus «سَلَٰمٌ هِىَ» izhar and «مَطْلَعِ» qalqalah.

questions.q: Extend: recite Al-Qadr to a partner who ticks each rule on your map.
Stretch: why is Al-Qadr a good 'model surah' for checking tajweed?
questions.a: It is short but contains most of the rules; a teacher can hear many rules in one minute.
A) qalqalah, because it is sakin. ط is a qalqalah letter; here it has sukoon.

questions.q: Think again: Al-Qadr has only five ayat. How many tajweed rules do you think you can find in it?
questions.a: More than ten: ghunnah, several madd families, heavy letters, qalqalah, ikhfa' and idgham.
